title: `completion/complete`
description: Returns autocomplete suggestions for a prompt argument or a resource template variable, capped at 100 values per response.
question: Can the framework ask the server to complete an argument value?
why: Completion is what makes prompt arguments and resource templates usable by a human rather than only by a program that already knows the valid values.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0: `MCPClient` does not wrap completion. The SDK client's `complete` sits behind the private `mcpClientsById` field.
notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: the adapter has no completion API. `MCPServer.session.complete(...)` works on the raw mcp `ClientSession`.
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: `MCPToolset` has no completion API. `toolset.client.complete(...)` works on the FastMCP client the toolset exposes.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` has no completion method, and the `ClientSession` it would need runs privately on the client's background thread (`_background_thread_session`), so a caller has no route to `completion/complete`.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `MCPServer` has no completion method. The MCP client's `complete` sits in the protected `session` field, so it is not a route a user is given.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` has no completion method; `completion/complete` works only through `MCPTools.session`, the fastmcp `Client` it exposes (`Client.complete`).
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy has no completion API. `completion/complete` works only through `complete` on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter` has no completion method. `completion/complete` is reachable only on the `@modelcontextprotocol/client` `Client` that `getClient(server)` hands out.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): there is no completion API. Nothing in `CopilotSession` or `session.rpc.mcp` sends `completion/complete` to an MCP server.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpClient` has no `completion/complete` method, so `DefaultMcpClient` never sends one.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `Complete` on.
